svg.title: Exact coverage of two binomial intervals against the true p
svg.desc: Coverage of the Wald and likelihood-ratio recipes at n equal to twenty, plotted against the true success probability, with a horizontal line at the nominal 0.95. The Wald curve collapses near zero and one. A second panel magnifies the left end.
svg.text: The stated 95 percent is a promise the Wald recipe does not keep
Exact coverage at n = 20, summed over all twenty-one possible counts, for every true value of p.
the same two curves, magnified over the range the worked example sits in
at p = 0.15 the Wald recipe covers 0.819
Both curves saw up and down because the data are discrete: as p slides, whole counts enter and
leave the covering set and the coverage jumps. That sawtooth is unavoidable for a discrete
model, and no recipe built on twenty-one possible outcomes can hold 0.95 exactly. What is
avoidable is the Wald curve's collapse toward the ends, where its intervals run outside the unit
Averaged over p between zero and one, the Wald recipe covers about 0.85 and the likelihood-ratio
recipe about 0.95. The likelihood-ratio curve dips too, near p = 0.09, but it dips to about 0.82
